Replies.Text:
Formalized from your notes (revision 4). What is yours to decide, each with my recommendation; resolve with no reply to take them all.

1. **Who resolves.** The thread's starter or an Owner of the project. Recommendation: yes; the asker knows when it is answered, the Owner can always close.
2. **No vote.** Consensus stays one person's acceptance of the last reply's outcome; a per-project 'Owners resolve everything' switch is left for a team that asks. Recommendation: no vote.
3. **Who a thread waits on.** Contested: starter, Owners and those who replied, minus the last speaker. Resolved: starter and Owners. Recommendation: as written; it keeps bystanders out of the counts.
4. **Who applies.** Anyone with write access, by Answer or by token; Answer comes to mean 'answer what waits on me, as me'. Recommendation: yes; it is the only reading once an LLM is never a user, and LLM Tasks gets the wording when its two waiting threads are applied.
5. **State by Owners only.** Draft to Plan, Plan to Working, Working to Finished are an Owner's; today anyone. Recommendation: yes; it is the counterweight to the starter resolving.
6. **One run per plan at a time**, the rest queued. Recommendation: yes; two runs on one plan would trip each other on the revision check.

Replies.Text:
One rule the read-through found wanting, with a recommendation; resolve with no reply to take it and I write it in.

**Who counts as the last speaker when a run spoke.** A run is the presser's, so when Andre presses Enhance and the LLM opens a question thread, the thread's starter and last speaker is Andre. Under "everyone who has replied, minus the last speaker", the thread then waits on the Owners and anyone else, but not on Andre, who is the one the question was for. The same happens on every Answer run: the LLM's reply as Andre stops the thread waiting on Andre.

Recommendation: for turn-taking, a speaker is the byline, not the account: "Claude-CLI by Andre" and "Andre" are two speakers. A thread a run opened for Andre waits on Andre; Andre's own reply waits on the others and on his connection, which Answer serves. Permissions stay the account's; only the waiting rule reads the pair. This keeps today's person-and-LLM back-and-forth working inside one account, which is what a single user on a Local server is.

Alternative: a run's threads and replies count as the presser's for waiting too, and Enhance's questions are read in the plan rather than waited on. Simpler, but the waiting list goes quiet exactly when the person is wanted.

Contested: the starter, the Owners, everyone who has replied in it, and the LLM speakers, minus the one who replied last; a person who has not joined in is not waited on. Resolved, waiting to be applied: the starter and the Owners. Applied: nobody. The speakers of a plan (`Participants.SeenSpeakers`) now carry the Owners of the plan's project, read from its Owners folder through the registry, each marked `Owner`, and the server's owner is marked the same; a speaker seen in the threads is `llm` when its byline has a service in it ("Claude-CLI by user") and `user` when it is a bare name.
- **Apply by write access.** `MayApply`: the owner, an Owner, a Member or a Service account; a Watcher is refused 403 with "applying a thread takes write access", before the 409s for a thread that is not resolved or already applied.
- **The State by Owners.** `MaySetState`: the owner or an Owner; `PUT /plans/:id/state` and a `State` given on `POST /plans` answer 403 "only an Owner sets a plan's State" to anyone else. The value check (`CanSetState`) is unchanged.

Without this, a fresh thread on a Local server would wait on nobody.
2. *An account acting for a person serves the resolved threads waiting on that person.* "Answer answers the threads waiting on the presser, as the presser: applies the resolved ones." So `/api/waiting`, the `mine` filter and `WaitingOnMe` list, for a run or an agent session, the threads waiting on its byline and the resolved ones waiting on its presser; the contested ones waiting on the presser stay the presser's own to answer (`WaitingOn`'s `Person`). It is what keeps the tools' `waiting` and my own turn working: a thread you resolve waits on you, and I apply it for you.

**What you will see.** A thread you resolve now waits on you (to apply, through Answer or me) rather than on the LLM, so it counts in "waiting on you" at the top of the plan; the line still says "N contested, waiting on you M", and M now includes the resolved ones, which reads oddly. Step 2 (the page) should move "waiting on you" out of the contested part. Old threads whose records carry a bare service name as `By` (the `llm` participant from before User Management Step 2) now count as a person's speaker: waited on only in the threads it replied in; all of those are finished plans.

**Build log, Step 3** (Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-21). The run queue; nothing committed. Resolve to accept, and on your turn I commit as "Multiuser Step 3" and bring the Readme document up to it.

**What was built.**
- **One run per plan at a time, and one per connection** (`src/Runs.js`). A press while its plan or its connection has a run on is not refused (the 409 of Run Shapes is gone): its record is made at once with `Status queued`, `Queued` the time of the press and `Behind` the run it waits for (id, task, plan), answered 201 and told so. Runs on other plans through other connections go together. The line is in press order: a press waits behind an earlier queued one on the same plan or connection too.
- **Its turn.** When a run ends, every queued run whose plan and connection are free starts. A queued run is **packaged again** then (`Runner` hands `Runs.Start` a `Prepare` that rebuilds the prompt and does the git pull), since the earlier run on the plan has changed it; the token minted at the press stays the run's. A package that fails then fails the run without starting it. Stop takes a queued run out of the line (stopped, "stopped before it started"); a queued run is not deleted; a run left queued by a server that stopped is closed at the next start. The runs list is in press order.
- **The page.** The toast on the plan heading and the LLM page says "Work queued on claude-cli behind Answer on The plan"; a queued run's row reads queued with when it was pressed and "queued since"; its popup has a Queued line with what it waits for and a Stop that takes it out of the line; a queued event leaves the connection's running mark alone.
- **The API guide, the README's API table and the LLM guide** say it; the docs are rebuilt.

**One reading I took.** The connection's one-at-a-time stays (a connection is one command or one model) and the queue sits in front of both limits, so "runs on different plans go together" when they are on different connections; a second plan on the same connection waits behind the first. If a connection should run two plans at once, that is a connection setting for later.

**Found on the way.** The smoke checked the tree's open rows with no wait; the plan lists come a moment later now that their summaries await the project's Owners (Step 1), so the check waits for the rows first. The browser suite's Escape-closes-Settings check failed twice under load and passed alone; nothing in this step touches it.
